 Clocks Have Fallen Back in the US and Europe: New Time Gaps for Filipino BPO Workers and OFW Families Hold Until March 2027
 by Plentisoft
 Nov 21, 2026 11:04 pm 
 Manila is now 13 hours ahead of New York and 8 hours ahead of London, while the gap to the Gulf and most of Asia is unchanged. 
 MANILA, Philippines, November 21, 2026 -- Daylight saving time has ended in the United States and Canada, where clocks fell back on November 1, and in Europe, where they changed on October 25. Because the Philippines keeps Philippine Standard Time (UTC+8) all year round, the time difference between Manila and these regions has grown by one hour. According to OnlineTimeNow , a free website of browser-based time tools, the new gaps will stay in place until clocks move forward again on March 14, 2027 in the US and Canada and on March 28, 2027 in Europe.
 The change matters most for the country's IT-BPM industry, which employs nearly two million people, many of them on shifts built around North American business hours. A shift that started at 9:00 p.m. Manila time to meet a 9:00 a.m. start in New York in October now begins at 10:00 p.m. For teams that support clients on the US West Coast, Manila is now 16 hours ahead of Los Angeles.
 Overseas Filipino workers and their families are affected too. Relatives in the US, Canada, the United Kingdom and Italy are now one hour further behind Manila, so regular video calls need to move. The gap to the Gulf states, Hong Kong, Singapore and Japan has not changed, because none of them change their clocks. Australia is the exception in the other direction: Sydney began its summer time on October 4 and is now three hours ahead of Manila instead of two, until April 4, 2027.
 How far ahead is Manila now? 
 Hours that Manila is ahead of each city, before and after the clock changes:
 Differences calculated from the IANA time zone database. Highlighted rows changed this autumn. 
 "Twice a year, many people in the Philippines discover that the time difference with their client or their family is not fixed,” said a spokesperson for OnlineTimeNow. "The Philippines does not change its clocks, so it is always the other side that moves. A one-hour shift is easy to miss, and it is enough to make you late for a client call or wake a relative in the middle of the night.”
 OnlineTimeNow's page on the current time in the Philippines shows the live local time for more than 150 Philippine cities, together with the clock changes coming up in other countries. The site also offers a free world clock, a time zone converter and an online alarm clock, all of which run in the browser without an app or an account.
 Three quick checks after a clock change 
 Confirm meeting times with overseas clients. Calendar invites usually adjust on their own, but shift rosters and recurring calls arranged by message often do not.
 Re-set your alarms for the new shift start. If your shift moved by an hour, your wake-up time and commute should move with it.
 Mark March 14 and March 28, 2027. On those dates the gaps with North America and Europe shrink by one hour again.
 About OnlineTimeNow 
 OnlineTimeNow (onlinetime.now) is a free collection of browser-based time tools, including an online alarm clock, timers, a stopwatch, a world clock, a time zone converter and date calculators. The tools need no download or account, keep users' alarms and settings in their own browser, and are available in 11 languages. Time zone offsets come from the IANA time zone database used by web browsers and operating systems.
